Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.

claims.assertion: The trip ran 20.1 km against a 15.5 km optimal route, +4.6 km (+30%), which exceeds the 1 km RD-1 tolerance, so the deviation is refundable unless a segment is exempt.

The single off-route segment 12:46–13:07 drove 9.70 km where the optimal route covers 5.62 km, adding 4.08 km, and it strayed up to 1720 m from the optimal route — well beyond map-matching noise (0.2 km).
The rider never consented to the reroute: there are no in-app chat messages at all on this trip, so no rider message before or at the deviation named a road, a stop or any route choice.

The driver's written statement — 'I followed my GPS, it took me off at Paya Lebar' — is made after the trip and offers no in-app or verbally recorded notice before the deviation; verbal notice needs a call recording and there is none.

No traffic justification exists for leaving the PIE at Paya Lebar: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route (F12), the PIE ran at speed band 7 / 60–69 km/h (F10) and the CXE at band 7 (F9) during the segment, and weather was fair (F13) — only Paya Lebar Road itself was moderately slow at band 4, which is not a closure, incident or heavy congestion on the replaced part of the route.
Because there is no traffic reason, RD-2 requires the excess distance fare to be refunded as refund_partial and a driver violation to be recorded.

The refund is computable from the fare record: 4.61 km of excess distance at $1.4099/km = $6.50, matching the billed excess distance (F4); tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded and surge is 1.0× here (F5).
No rider message having exempted any part of the segment, none of the 4.08 km segment addition is exempt under RD-3 or RD-5, so the full billed excess distance of $6.50 is refundable.

The driver should also receive a notification-duty reminder and the notification failure should be logged on the driver's route compliance record; no formal warning is due as this is a first such incident for this driver (0 upheld route violations in 90 days).
The amount in dispute ($6.50) is under $10, so under TH-1 this is a final system ruling, and no records needed for the route analysis are missing.

weaknesses: The billed excess distance in F4 (4.61 km / $6.50) is slightly larger than the segment addition in F3 (4.08 km); the driver's advocate will argue the refundable km should be capped at 4.08 km (about $5.75) rather than the full $6.50, and that F1's 20.1 km figure rounds F6's 20.08 km.
The rider's own profile (F14: 5 disputes in 90 days, 3 upheld, all route) will be used to paint the rider as a serial claimant, and could be argued as a credibility factor under TH-3.

F11 (Paya Lebar Road speed band 4 during 12:45–13:15) lets the driver argue there was congestion on the road he actually took, though RD-4 requires the congestion to be on the replaced part of the recommended route, which F9/F10/F12 show was free-flowing with no incidents.

There is no record of what the rider did or said in the car; if the driver produces a call recording or an unrecorded verbal exchange, the RD-5 analysis changes, but on the present record the driver's statement F8 is a post-trip claim only.

claims.assertion: The trip ran 20.1 km against an optimal 15.5 km, so the deviation is 4.6 km and exceeds the 1 km tolerance; some refund exposure is unavoidable on this record.

Only one off-route segment exists (12:46–13:07), covering 9.70 km where the optimal route covers 5.62 km and adding 4.08 km, all of it on named public roads from Paya Lebar through Eunos and Siglap to Bedok North Avenue 1 — no stop or detour to a place of the driver's own appears anywhere in the record.

There is no rider consent of any kind: the chat record is empty and the driver's written statement is post-trip only, so the segment cannot be exempted under RD-5 — the driver does not contest that notice was not given.

No traffic reason supports the reroute: the road the driver left, the PIE, ran at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and the CTE at band 7 throughout, no incident was recorded near the route, and the weather was fair — the only slow road (Paya Lebar Road, band 4) is on the deviation, not on the replaced part of the optimal route.

Because there is no traffic reason and no rider agreement, the refund is limited to the excess distance fare — tolls, time fare and surge are not refundable — which the fare record puts at $6.50 (4.61 km × $1.4099/km).

The driver's clean record (4.8 rating, 640 trips in 90 days, zero upheld disputes) means RD-6's repeat-violation add-on does not apply and no flag_account is warranted; this is a first, non-repeating routing incident.

No safety element arises anywhere in the complaint, chat or statement: there is no allegation of dangerous driving, threat or harassment, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged and this remains a fare-calculation dispute.
The amount in dispute is under $10, so the system decides it finally without human review.

weaknesses: The core facts are against the driver: F1 shows +4.6 km over 15.5 km optimal and F3 shows a single 4.08 km-adding off-route segment running 1720 m off the optimal route, so the RD-1 tolerance is clearly blown and some refund is inevitable.

There is no rider consent at all — F7 records no in-app chat and F8 is a post-trip statement, which RD-5 expressly excludes ("the driver's word alone does not count"), so every segment ground is consent_after_or_none.
No traffic justification is available: F10 (PIE band 7) and F12 (no incidents) defeat RD-4, so RD-2's no-traffic-reason row applies and a driver violation is recorded as well as the refund.

The rider's profile (F14: 5 disputes in 90 days, 3 upheld on route) lets the other side argue a pattern on the rider's part, but it cannot rebut the GPS facts, and the driver's own F8 statement "I followed my GPS" concedes the reroute happened.

points.response: Agreed — the condition is not in dispute: F1 shows +4.6 km against a 15.5 km optimal route, far past the 1 km tolerance in RD-1, so a refund follows.

Agreed as far as it goes: F3 shows one off-route segment at 12:46–13:07 adding 4.08 km and wandering up to 1720 m off the optimal route, and nothing in the record shows a stop or errand of the driver's own — but that only means the ground is consent_after_or_none under RD-5, not that the kilometres are exempt.

Conceded: F7 records no in-app chat at all and F8 is a post-trip statement, which RD-5 excludes, so no segment ground other than consent_after_or_none is available and none of the 4.08 km segment addition is exempt under RD-3 or RD-5.

Agreed: F10 (PIE band 7), F9 (CTE band 7), F12 (no incidents) and F13 (fair weather) defeat RD-4, and F11's band 4 on Paya Lebar Road is congestion on the deviation, not on 'the replaced part of the recommended route' that RD-4 requires.

Agreed on the measure and the amount: F4 gives $6.50 as 4.61 km × $1.4099/km and F6 confirms the components are base, distance, time, platform only with surge at 1.0× (F5), so $6.50 is the refundable excess distance fare under RD-2 and nothing more is claimed for tolls, time or surge.

Agreed that no flag_account is sought: F15 shows a clean 90-day record with 0 upheld route violations, so RD-6's repeat-deviation add-on does not apply and only RD-7's notification reminder and compliance log are asked for.

Agreed: the complaint, the empty chat (F7) and the driver's statement (F8) contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1 is not engaged and this stays a fare-calculation dispute.
Agreed: the disputed amount in F4 is $6.50, under $10, so TH-1/TH-2 make this a final system ruling, which is why the rider asks for refund_partial of $6.50 on the RD-2 no-traffic-reason row.
Conceded: F1 does show +4.6 km over the 15.5 km optimal route, over the 1 km RD-1 tolerance, and we do not dispute that some refund is payable.
Conceded: F3 shows one off-route segment 12:46–13:07 driving 9.70 km against 5.62 km optimal and adding 4.08 km, far beyond the 0.2 km noise floor; our own brief states the same ground.

Conceded: F7 records no in-app chat at all, so no rider message before or at the deviation named a road, stop or route choice; that is why we record the segment ground as consent_after_or_none rather than an exempt ground.

We do not defend notice: F8 is a post-trip statement and RD-5 requires in-app chat or a call recording before or at the point of deviation, so the segment is not exempt — but F8's content ('it took me off at Paya Lebar') shows the driver followed the navigation device rather than making a detour to a place of his own.

Conceded: F10 shows the PIE free-flowing at band 7, F12 records no incidents and F13 fair weather, so no RD-4 traffic reason exists; F11's slow Paya Lebar Road is on the deviation itself, not on the replaced part of the optimal route.
Conceded as to the refund row and the recorded violation: with no traffic reason, RD-2 gives refund_partial of the excess distance fare and a driver violation entry.
Conceded on the arithmetic: F4 gives 4.61 km at $1.4099/km = $6.50 and F5 confirms surge 1.0×, refundable only as excess distance fare.

Partly contested: the rider's own concession shows F4's 4.61 km exceeds F3's 4.08 km segment addition, and RD-2 refunds the excess distance attributable to the deviation, so the refundable figure is $5.75 (4.08 km × $1.4099/km) with the balance of the meter difference not arising from the off-route segment.

Conceded: RD-7 applies and a notification-duty reminder with a log entry is appropriate; we only note F15 shows a 4.8-rated driver with 640 trips and zero upheld route disputes, so no formal warning and no flag_account under RD-6.
Conceded: the disputed sum is under $10 and the GPS, fare and chat records are complete, so TH-1/TH-2 give a final system ruling on this file with no escalation needed.

notices.text:

This was decided on the trip's distance data. Your route was about 4.6 km longer than the shortest reasonable route, and the off-route stretch was not explained by any traffic condition on the roads it replaced — it also wasn't caused by anything you asked for, since you sent no message about the route during the trip.

Tolls, time fare and surge are not part of this refund. No flag has been placed on your account.

The dispute on this trip is resolved against the route taken: $6.50 of excess distance fare is being refunded to the rider's original payment method.

The distance records show the trip ran about 4.6 km longer than the shortest reasonable route, and the off-route stretch is not supported by any traffic condition on the roads it replaced. There was no rider message about the route before that stretch, so it does not count as agreed.

You'll get a notification-duty reminder, and this is logged on your route compliance record as a first incident — no formal warning, no account flag.
